metadata.methods_description: 64-channel EEG data were recorded using actively amplified wet electrodes in the 10-20 system referenced to FCz, along with ECG (right clavicle and left shinbone) and EDA (middle and ring fingers of the non-dominant hand) using BrainAmp DC amplifiers (BrainProducts GmbH). Data were sampled at 500 Hz with 16-bit resolution and a 0.016 Hz high-pass filter. Participants viewed 56 Streetview images and rated each on 9 scales across two blocks separated by a break, with EEG, ECG, and EDA recorded throughout.

funding.funder_name: This Study was realized by funding from the Berlin University Alliance.

citation_details.title: UREEF
citation_details.author: Weishan Bai, Wenyu Zhang
citation_details.abstract: The analysis code for this study is organized into six Jupyter Notebooks, covering SEED-IV data processing and CA-EEGNet training (UREEF01), ENS construction and visualization (UREEF02), Urban Appraisal image processing and semantic segmentation (UREEF03), Urban Appraisal EEG preprocessing (UREEF04), ENS-based projection and transfer analysis (UREEF05), and stimulus-level association analysis between ENS-derived scores and urban scene composition (UREEF06).The code is written in Python 3.11 and is intended to be run in Google Colab or Jupyter Notebook. The analyses rely on two third-party open-access datasets. The SEED-IV dataset is available at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/phhasian0710/seed-iv and may require registration for access. The Urban Appraisal dataset (OpenNeuro ds006850) is available at https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds006850/versions/1.0.0 under the CC BY 4.0 license.
